How this is resolved

Everyone who has served as White House Press Secretary at any time in Trump's second term counts, including those who served before these markets opened. Trump's second term began on Jan 20, 2025 and ends on Jan 20, 2029.
Anyone who holds the role only in an acting or interim capacity does NOT count. If that person is later formally named White House Press Secretary, they count.
Each person counts once, even if they serve more than once.
Markets may resolve as soon as the number of people who count reaches the strike.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of days Trump's next White House Press Secretary serves is at least 7 days before they leave the role or their departure is announced, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The next Press Secretary is the first person, after Issuance, to formally hold the position of White House Press Secretary, as formally designated by the White House. Acting and interim Press Secretaries do not count, and time served in an acting or interim capacity is not counted.

The count starts on the first day they serve as White House Press Secretary in a non-acting capacity. That can be the day they are named, if they take up the role that day, but never earlier. If no first day is reported, it is the earlier of their first White House briefing as Press Secretary and the first day the White House publicly identifies them as Press Secretary.

The count ends on whichever of these comes first:

The day they leave the role for any reason, including resignation, removal or moving to another role in which they no longer hold the title of White House Press Secretary
The day the President, the White House or the Press Secretary says publicly that they are leaving or have been removed, including by naming someone else to replace them, or a Source Agency first reports this citing a White House or administration official

A statement that they may leave, should reconsider or are under review does not end the count. A Press Secretary still serving when Trump's term ends on Jan 20, 2029 leaves the role that day.

The number of days is the number of calendar days (Eastern Time) from the first day to the end day. A Press Secretary whose first day is Nov 1, 2026 and whose departure is announced on Nov 11, 2026 has served 10 days. The Exchange computes the count from the first day and end day as defined here; a tenure length stated in reporting does not determine the count. If no new Press Secretary begins serving before Jan 20, 2029, the number of days is zero.
markets.title: Will the number of days Trump's next White House Press Secretary serves be at least 7 before they leave the role or their departure is announced?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the House adopts an article of impeachment against Donald Trump.
markets.rules_primary: If the number of Republican Representatives voting Yea on the first House vote to impeach Donald Trump is at least 1 during his second term as President, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The first vote that counts is the first recorded House vote in which the House adopts a resolution or an article of impeachment against Donald Trump. If the articles are voted on separately, the vote on the first article adopted counts.

Only Yea votes by Representatives listed as Republicans in the Clerk of the House's roll call for that vote count.

Does NOT count:

A vote on a motion to table, refer, postpone or otherwise dispose of an impeachment resolution
A vote on a resolution or article that the House does not adopt
A committee vote

Donald Trump must be in office as President when the article is adopted. If the House does not adopt an article of impeachment against him during that period, the number is zero.

markets.rules_primary: If the third-party share of the national popular vote for President is at least 1% in the 2028 U.S. presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Third-party votes are all votes cast for President other than votes for the Democratic nominee and the Republican nominee. They include votes for independent and minor-party candidates, write-in votes, and votes for "None of these candidates."

A nominee is the candidate the Democratic Party or the Republican Party nominated for President. A nominee's votes on every ballot line are combined, including a line of another party (such as New York's Conservative and Working Families lines), and are not third-party votes.

The third-party share is the third-party votes divided by the total votes cast for President in the 50 states and the District of Columbia, using the Federal Election Commission's "Official Presidential General Election Results" for the Nov 7, 2028 election: (Total Votes minus the Democratic nominee's total minus the Republican nominee's total) divided by Total Votes. Blank and spoiled ballots are not counted. Votes the report does not include, such as write-ins a state does not tally, are not added from other sources. In a state that uses ranked-choice voting, first-round votes are used.

The first version of the report that the FEC publishes is used; later revisions do not count. Each state's figures are its final certified results, including a recount completed before certification. If the FEC has not published the report by expiration, the sum of the states' and the District of Columbia's final certified results is used.
markets.title: Will the third-party share of the 2028 presidential popular vote be at least 1%?

Third-party votes are all votes cast for President other than votes for the Democratic nominee and the Republican nominee. They include votes for independent and minor-party candidates, write-in votes, and votes for "None of these candidates."

A nominee is the candidate the Democratic Party or the Republican Party nominated for President. A nominee's votes on every ballot line are combined, including a line of another party (such as New York's Conservative and Working Families lines), and are not third-party votes.

The third-party share is the third-party votes divided by the total votes cast for President in the 50 states and the District of Columbia, using the Federal Election Commission's "Official Presidential General Election Results" for the Nov 7, 2028 election: (Total Votes minus the Democratic nominee's total minus the Republican nominee's total) divided by Total Votes. Blank and spoiled ballots are not counted. Votes the report does not include, such as write-ins a state does not tally, are not added from other sources. In a state that uses ranked-choice voting, first-round votes are used.

The first version of the report that the FEC publishes is used; later revisions do not count. Each state's figures are its final certified results, including a recount completed before certification. If the FEC has not published the report by expiration, the sum of the states' and the District of Columbia's final certified results is used.
markets.title: Will the third-party share of the 2028 presidential popular vote be at least 3%?

markets.rules_primary: If anyone other than the Democratic or Republican nominee wins the most votes for President in at least one state or the District of Columbia in the Nov 7, 2028 U.S. presidential election, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A state or the District of Columbia is counted when the candidate with the most votes statewide in its certified results is neither the Democratic Party's nor the Republican Party's nominee for President. Write-in candidates count. Electoral votes, including any cast by unpledged or faithless electors, do NOT decide a state's winner.

A party's nominee is the candidate that party officially nominates for President. A nominee who is also listed under another party's line, such as the Working Families Party in New York, is still that party's nominee and does NOT count as independent or third party. A candidate who is endorsed by either party but is not its nominee counts. A candidate listed on a state's ballot as the Democratic or Republican candidate in place of that party's nominee does NOT count.

In Maine and Nebraska, only the statewide vote counts. In a state that counts ranked-choice ballots, such as Maine, the candidate with the most votes is the one leading the final round of the certified tabulation. Winning a congressional district does NOT count.

Resolution is based on certified results only, not preliminary results.

This market is based on the Bureau of Economic Analysis’s advance estimate of real gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the United States for calendar year 2028. The Expiration Value will be the first-published annual percent change in real GDP for 2028 from BEA’s GDP release, expected with the advance estimate of Q4 2028 GDP in early 2029. Revisions published after expiration will not be considered.

All stated bounds are inclusive. For example, “5.6% to 6.0%” includes both 5.6% and 6.0%, “6.1% or above” includes 6.1%, and “0.0% or below” includes 0.0%.

Rankings are determined by total seat count after the election, including holdover seats not up for election.

Coalitions, power-sharing agreements and the election of chamber leaders do NOT count.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. goods and services deficit for calendar year 2028 is strictly above $500 billion dollars, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Underlying is the nominal goods and services balance on a balance-of-payments basis. It will not use the goods-only deficit, the advance goods report, the December monthly deficit, or inflation-adjusted trade data.

Because the agencies generally report the balance as a negative number, the market will use the absolute size of the deficit. For example, an annual trade balance of −$800.1 billion constitutes a trade deficit of $800.1 billion.

Resolution will use the first annual estimate published in the release covering December of 2028. Subsequent annual revisions will not be considered.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If U.S. Senator is an office previously held by the first person inaugurated as President for the term beginning January 20, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This must be confirmed, verified, or established as factual by at least one Source Agency.

Each market resolves independently and more than one can resolve YES.

"Previously held" means the person was sworn in and served in the office at any time before January 20, 2029. Any length of service counts, and it does not matter whether the person reached the office through election, appointment or succession. A person who was elected or appointed but never sworn in did NOT hold the office.

What each office means:

President: President of the United States. Serving as Acting President under Section 3 of the 25th Amendment does NOT count.
Vice President: Vice President of the United States.
U.S. Senator: a United States Senator. A state senator does NOT count.
U.S. Representative: a voting member of the United States House of Representatives. A state representative, a territorial Delegate and the Resident Commissioner of Puerto Rico do NOT count.
Governor: Governor of one of the 50 states or of a United States territory, including a person who succeeded to the office. A Lieutenant Governor temporarily discharging the Governor's duties does NOT count.
Mayor: Mayor of any incorporated municipality in the United States, of any population, including in an acting or interim capacity. A city council or county governing board office does NOT count.
Cabinet Secretary: a Senate-confirmed head of one of the 15 executive departments, including the Attorney General. An acting head does NOT count, and neither does a Cabinet-rank official who does not head an executive department, such as the U.S. Trade Representative or the Director of National Intelligence.
State Legislator: a member of either chamber of the legislature of one of the 50 states.
markets.title: Will it be confirmed that U.S. Senator is an office previously held by the first person inaugurated as President for the term beginning January 20, 2029?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if complete Federal Register data becomes available.
markets.rules_primary: If the President signs below 300 Executive Orders during his second term, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: An Executive Order must be formally titled "Executive Order" followed by a number, signed by the President, and published in the Federal Register. Presidential Memoranda, Proclamations, Determinations, and other executive actions that are not formally numbered Executive Orders do not count. The signing date as recorded in the Federal Register determines which period an Executive Order belongs to, using ET timezone. Classified Executive Orders count if acknowledged by number. Executive Orders that are later revoked still count for the period they were signed. The Federal Register is the primary source; alternative sources are used only if the Federal Register explicitly states data is incomplete.
markets.title: Will the President sign fewer than 300 Executive Orders between Jan 20, 2025 and Jan 20, 2029?

markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic Party holds more seats than any other party in the Hawaii Senate after the Hawaii legislative election held on November 7, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Rankings are determined by total seat count after the election, including holdover seats not up for election.

Each member is counted once, for the party designation shown by the State of Hawaii (for holdover members, as of the date of the general election). Events after the date of the general election, such as party switches, deaths, resignations, vacancies, appointments, special elections, and any decision by the Hawaii Senate to refuse to seat or to expel a member-elect, are disregarded. Independent and unaffiliated members do NOT count for any party, even if they caucus with one.

Coalitions, power-sharing agreements and the election of chamber leaders do NOT count.

In case of exact ties, markets resolve proportionally (1/number of tied parties).

This market is eligible for accelerated determination after a consensus of media organizations project that a party has won a majority of the seats in the Hawaii Senate.

markets.rules_secondary: A stake announced before the deadline counts, even if the deal closes after it. Taking a stake means acquiring direct equity ownership, voting shares, or equivalent ownership interests. Ownership is aggregated across all share classes and listings. Crossing the threshold at any point satisfies the criterion regardless of subsequent changes. Non-equity instruments like bonds or loans don't qualify. Stakes by sovereign wealth funds or state-owned enterprises attributed to the body count. The value can be expressed as percentage ownership, monetary value, or share count, with percentage being the default unless specified.

markets.rules_primary: If President Donald Trump makes a recess appointment after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

A recess appointment means an appointment to a position that would otherwise require Senate confirmation, made using the power given to the President in the recess appointments clause (Article II, Section 2, Clause 3) of the Constitution. One appointee is enough. If an appointment is later ruled illegal by the Supreme Court of the United States, or another federal court, this market's resolution will not change.

An acting official designated under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act does NOT count.

markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. Department of the Treasury announces its completed purchase of Bitcoin for a government-held reserve or stockpile before Jan 21, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A purchase means the named cryptocurrency acquired for value and held by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, including units bought with the proceeds of selling other digital assets already held. The announcement must state that the purchase has been made. Each strike settles on its own token, and more than one strike can resolve YES.

The following do NOT count:
An intended, planned or authorized purchase, including one authorized by legislation or by executive order
Units confiscated pursuant to criminal or civil enforcement proceedings, or otherwise received rather than bought
Exchange-traded products, futures or other derivative exposure

This market resolves based on when the departure is publicly announced or officially communicated, regardless of the effective date. The first official is the one whose announcement or departure comes first after Issuance. If a single announcement covers both named officials, the market will resolve to 1 / N where N is the number of named officials covered by that announcement.

Leaving means ceasing to be Secretary of State, for Marco Rubio, or Secretary of Defense, for Pete Hegseth, by resignation, firing, removal or a move to another post; a change in the name of the office is not leaving. Leaving only another role, such as National Security Advisor, a temporary leave or recusal, being considered for another position, and impeachment without removal do NOT count. A departure that takes effect at the end of the current presidential term on Jan 20, 2029 does NOT count, including a statement that he will not serve in the next administration.

No officials will be added to this event. None resolves to Yes if neither named official leaves or announces he will leave his position before Jan 20, 2029.

Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.
markets.title: Will it be reported by any of the Source Agencies that Marco Rubio is the first of the two officials named in this event to leave, or announce he will leave, his position as Secretary of State before Jan 20, 2029?

markets.rules_primary: If CMS announces the addition of GLP-1 drugs for obesity to Part D before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
GLP-1 drugs are already covered under Part D for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk reduction and obstructive sleep apnea. Those indications are outside this market, which turns on coverage for obesity or chronic weight management.

Only a completed CMS action that provides the coverage counts, such as a final rule, a finalized model design, or guidance to Part D sponsors through the Health Plan Management System. Where the White House or HHS makes the determination, the CMS document adopting it resolves this market, on the date of that document.

The following do NOT resolve this market to YES:
A CMS communication that discusses, studies or reports on such coverage.
A proposed rule or a request for applications, which propose coverage rather than provide it.
An action that considers the change and declines to make it.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, or extending or replacing it, because it sits outside the Part D benefit.
An announcement covering only the Medicaid portion of the BALANCE Model.

Coverage of a single drug, or of a subset of Part D enrollees, is sufficient. The announcement date governs, not the date coverage takes effect.
markets.title: Will CMS announce the addition of GLP-1 drugs for obesity to Part D before Jan 1, 2027?

markets.rules_primary: If Alina Habba formally holds the position of White House Press Secretary before Jan 20, 2029, and is the first such subject to do so after Issuance, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The holder of the position at the time of Issuance is excluded.

For the purposes of this Contract, only a subject who holds the position in a permanent, confirmed, elected, or otherwise non-acting and non-temporary capacity, as formally designated by the body or organization at which the position is held, is treated as formally holding the position; assumption of the role solely in an acting, interim, transitional, provisional, caretaker, pro tempore, or otherwise temporary capacity does not, by itself, satisfy the Payout Criterion.

“No new person” resolves Yes only if no new person formally holds the position in a permanent capacity before Jan 20, 2029; in that case every other market resolves No.

markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic Party holds more seats than any other party in the West Virginia Senate after the West Virginia legislative election held on November 7, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Rankings are determined by total seat count after the election, including holdover seats not up for election.

Each member is counted once, for the party designation shown by the State of West Virginia (for holdover members, as of the date of the general election). Events after the date of the general election, such as party switches, deaths, resignations, vacancies, appointments, special elections, and any decision by the West Virginia Senate to refuse to seat or to expel a member-elect, are disregarded. Independent and unaffiliated members do NOT count for any party, even if they caucus with one.

Coalitions, power-sharing agreements and the election of chamber leaders do NOT count.

In case of exact ties, markets resolve proportionally (1/number of tied parties).

This market is eligible for accelerated determination after a consensus of media organizations project that a party has won a majority of the seats in the West Virginia Senate.
markets.title: Will the Democratic Party hold the most seats in the West Virginia State Senate after the 2028 election?

markets.rules_secondary:
Rankings are determined by total seat count after the election.

Each member is counted once, for the party designation shown by the State of North Carolina. Events after the date of the general election, such as party switches, deaths, resignations, vacancies, appointments, special elections, and any decision by the North Carolina Senate to refuse to seat or to expel a member-elect, are disregarded. Independent and unaffiliated members do NOT count for any party, even if they caucus with one.

Coalitions, power-sharing agreements and the election of chamber leaders do NOT count.

In case of exact ties, markets resolve proportionally (1/number of tied parties).

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if an Acquisition of Greenland occurs with a reported Total Monetary Consideration.
markets.rules_primary: If the Total Monetary Consideration for a U.S. Acquisition of Greenland is exactly $0 / No Acquisition during Trump's term, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An "Acquisition of Greenland" is any of the following, as reported by at least two Source Agencies:
The signing of a treaty, agreement, or compact between the United States and Denmark and/or Greenland that transfers sovereignty, territorial control, or administrative authority over all or substantially all of Greenland to the United States
U.S. Senate ratification of such a treaty or agreement
A formal announcement by the White House or the U.S. Department of State that Greenland has become a U.S. territory, insular area, or state
The entry into force of a Compact of Free Association, or a substantially similar agreement, between the United States and an independent Greenland that grants the United States exclusive military access and defense responsibility over Greenland

It does not include expanded base rights at Pituffik Space Base or other existing facilities without a broader sovereignty or Compact of Free Association agreement; trade agreements, economic partnerships, or investment treaties that do not transfer sovereignty, territorial control, or exclusive military access; informal statements of intent, non-binding memoranda of understanding, or preliminary negotiations; or military occupation or seizure of Greenland without such a formal agreement.

The Total Monetary Consideration is the total U.S. dollar value of everything the U.S. government announces, commits, or agrees to provide in connection with the Acquisition, including:
Cash payments, lump sum or in installments
The face value of U.S. Treasury securities or other government-issued bonds
Direct payments to Greenland residents (the per-person amount times the number of eligible recipients stated in the agreement, or times 57,000 if not stated)
Recurring economic assistance, grants, or subsidies over the full stated term (50 times the annual amount if the term is indefinite or longer than 50 years)
Infrastructure investment commitments stated in the agreement
Assumption of Greenland's or Denmark's existing debt stated in the agreement
Any other financial commitments in, or convertible to, U.S. dollars

It excludes the imputed value of military protection, defense guarantees, or security commitments; non-quantified promises of economic development, trade preferences, or market access; the value of citizenship, visa-free travel, or other non-monetary rights; the estimated value of natural resources, land, or strategic positioning; and anything paid or committed by parties other than the U.S. government. Amounts in other currencies are converted at the Federal Reserve H.10 rate on the announcement date. The total is rounded to the nearest $1 billion.

If Source Agencies report figures that conflict, the figure from the highest-ranked Source Agency that gives a specific amount is used, and a White House, State Department, or Treasury figure takes precedence over any media outlet. Revisions before expiration count; revisions after expiration do not. If an Acquisition occurs but no Source Agency gives a specific amount, the market resolves on an official figure published by any Source Agency within 90 days.

An agreement that is conditional on future events (such as an independence referendum, Danish parliamentary approval, or Senate ratification) counts when it is signed or announced, valued at its announced terms; if it lapses during Trump's term, it is treated as no Acquisition. If the Acquisition happens through several related agreements or phases, the consideration is summed across all of them first announced during Trump's term.

If no Acquisition of Greenland occurs and is reported by the U.S., Danish, or Greenlandic government during Trump's term, including if the United States takes military control of Greenland without a formal agreement, the "$0 / No Acquisition" market resolves Yes and every other market resolves No.
markets.title: Will there be no U.S. acquisition of Greenland during Trump's term?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if an Acquisition of Greenland occurs with a reported Total Monetary Consideration.
markets.rules_primary: If the Total Monetary Consideration for a U.S. Acquisition of Greenland is between $1 billion and $9 billion during Trump's term, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An "Acquisition of Greenland" is any of the following, as reported by at least two Source Agencies:
The signing of a treaty, agreement, or compact between the United States and Denmark and/or Greenland that transfers sovereignty, territorial control, or administrative authority over all or substantially all of Greenland to the United States
U.S. Senate ratification of such a treaty or agreement
A formal announcement by the White House or the U.S. Department of State that Greenland has become a U.S. territory, insular area, or state
The entry into force of a Compact of Free Association, or a substantially similar agreement, between the United States and an independent Greenland that grants the United States exclusive military access and defense responsibility over Greenland

It does not include expanded base rights at Pituffik Space Base or other existing facilities without a broader sovereignty or Compact of Free Association agreement; trade agreements, economic partnerships, or investment treaties that do not transfer sovereignty, territorial control, or exclusive military access; informal statements of intent, non-binding memoranda of understanding, or preliminary negotiations; or military occupation or seizure of Greenland without such a formal agreement.

The Total Monetary Consideration is the total U.S. dollar value of everything the U.S. government announces, commits, or agrees to provide in connection with the Acquisition, including:
Cash payments, lump sum or in installments
The face value of U.S. Treasury securities or other government-issued bonds
Direct payments to Greenland residents (the per-person amount times the number of eligible recipients stated in the agreement, or times 57,000 if not stated)
Recurring economic assistance, grants, or subsidies over the full stated term (50 times the annual amount if the term is indefinite or longer than 50 years)
Infrastructure investment commitments stated in the agreement
Assumption of Greenland's or Denmark's existing debt stated in the agreement
Any other financial commitments in, or convertible to, U.S. dollars

It excludes the imputed value of military protection, defense guarantees, or security commitments; non-quantified promises of economic development, trade preferences, or market access; the value of citizenship, visa-free travel, or other non-monetary rights; the estimated value of natural resources, land, or strategic positioning; and anything paid or committed by parties other than the U.S. government. Amounts in other currencies are converted at the Federal Reserve H.10 rate on the announcement date. The total is rounded to the nearest $1 billion.

If Source Agencies report figures that conflict, the figure from the highest-ranked Source Agency that gives a specific amount is used, and a White House, State Department, or Treasury figure takes precedence over any media outlet. Revisions before expiration count; revisions after expiration do not. If an Acquisition occurs but no Source Agency gives a specific amount, the market resolves on an official figure published by any Source Agency within 90 days.

An agreement that is conditional on future events (such as an independence referendum, Danish parliamentary approval, or Senate ratification) counts when it is signed or announced, valued at its announced terms; if it lapses during Trump's term, it is treated as no Acquisition. If the Acquisition happens through several related agreements or phases, the consideration is summed across all of them first announced during Trump's term.

If no Acquisition of Greenland occurs and is reported by the U.S., Danish, or Greenlandic government during Trump's term, including if the United States takes military control of Greenland without a formal agreement, the "$0 / No Acquisition" market resolves Yes and every other market resolves No.

markets.title: Will the U.S. pay between $1 billion and $9 billion for Greenland during Trump's term?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic Party holds more seats than any other party in the Georgia Senate after the Georgia legislative election held on November 7, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Rankings are determined by total seat count after the election.

Each member is counted once, for the party designation shown by the State of Georgia. Events after the date of the general election, such as party switches, deaths, resignations, vacancies, appointments, special elections, and any decision by the Georgia Senate to refuse to seat or to expel a member-elect, are disregarded. Independent and unaffiliated members do NOT count for any party, even if they caucus with one.

Coalitions, power-sharing agreements and the election of chamber leaders do NOT count.

In case of exact ties, markets resolve proportionally (1/number of tied parties).

This market is eligible for accelerated determination after a consensus of media organizations project that a party has won a majority of the seats in the Georgia Senate.
markets.title: Will the Democratic Party hold the most seats in the Georgia State Senate after the 2028 election?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Trump issues a single pardon that names at least 25 Trump administration staff, or that covers Trump administration staff as a group by role, agency, or policy area, before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market resolves to Yes if, during Trump's current Presidential term and before the deadline date, a single presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve names at least 25 Trump administration staff or covers Trump administration staff as a group by role, agency, or policy area.

Trump administration staff refers to officials and employees of the executive branch (the Executive Office of the President, the executive departments, federal agencies, and the armed forces) who served at any time after Jan 20, 2025. Contractors and other non-employees are not Trump administration staff.

A pardon covers staff as a group by role, agency, or policy area if it applies to everyone who held a role, worked at an agency, or worked on a policy, without naming each of them. The group must be defined by executive branch service. A single pardon is one proclamation, executive order, or warrant of clemency. A pardon counts even if no recipient has been charged with a crime, and even if a recipient rejects it.

Examples:
One proclamation pardoning all officers and employees of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement → resolves to Yes
One proclamation pardoning all federal personnel for conduct relating to immigration enforcement → resolves to Yes
One warrant naming 30 White House aides → resolves to Yes
40 separate warrants issued on the same day, each naming one aide → resolves to No

The following do NOT count:
Separate pardons that each name fewer than 25 staff, even if together they name more
Pardons defined only by an offense or event and open to people regardless of executive branch service, unless the pardon names at least 25 Trump administration staff
Pardons that cover only people whose executive branch service ended before Jan 20, 2025
State pardons
markets.title: Will Trump issue a blanket pardon for administration staff before Jan 1, 2027?

markets.rules_secondary:
The market resolves to Yes if the specified person receives a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve during the specified Presidential term and before the deadline date. The pardon can be for any federal crime. Commutations that reduce sentences and reprieves that delay punishment also satisfy the criterion. State-level pardons do not count. The Presidential term continues even if the President changes due to succession or resignation.

As of issuance, qualifying names include: Melania Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump, Jared Kushner, Eric Trump, Lara Trump, Tiffany Trump, Michael Boulos, Barron Trump, Elizabeth Trump Grau, James Walter Grau. Immediate family includes spouses, children, and siblings.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Supreme Court grants a writ of certiorari to any 3rd Amendment case before Jan 20, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The case must meet the following requirements: (1) The petition for certiorari explicitly raises a claim or question under the Third Amendment to the United States Constitution as a question presented; OR (2) The lower court decision being appealed explicitly addressed a Third Amendment claim on the merits; OR (3) The Supreme Court's order granting certiorari explicitly identifies a Third Amendment issue as a question for review. For the avoidance of doubt:  A case where the Third Amendment is mentioned only in passing, in dicta, or as part of a general constitutional analysis without being a distinct claim SHALL NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion A case where the Third Amendment is raised only in amicus briefs but not by the parties SHALL NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion. Examples that WOULD resolve to Yes: the Court grants cert in a case where a homeowner challenges military housing requirements under the Third Amendment; the Court grants cert in a case where the question presented is "Whether police officers qualify as 'soldiers' under the Third Amendment”; the Court grants cert where a lower court ruled on the scope of Third Amendment protections and that ruling is being appealed.
markets.title: What cases will the Supreme Court agree to hear before Jan 2029?

events.title: Will the Supreme Court hear a 3rd Amendment case before Trump's term ends?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the United States explicitly and formally recognizes Somaliland as a sovereign state independent from any previously recognized country after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This could include: opening a U.S. embassy with Somaliland, accepting an ambassador from Somaliland, including the entity as an independent country in U.S. Department of State country lists, or signing a formal treaty, bilateral agreement, or communique that explicitly identifies Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state.

Merely acknowledging a governing authority exists, without recognizing its authority, is insufficient to resolve the market to Yes. Establishing a consulate or liaison office without the formal status and language of recognition does not qualify. Trade offices, cultural centers, or other non-embassy missions are insufficient. Participation alongside the entity in international conferences, humanitarian aid missions, or multilateral forums does not in itself constitute recognition as a sovereign state. Nor does U.S. abstention or vote in an international organization automatically equate to bilateral recognition.
markets.title: Will Trump recognize Somaliland?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any leader in the set leaves office.
markets.rules_primary: If the individual holding the title of Secretary of Health and Human Services at the time of Issuance is the first within the HHS Secretary, the Secretary of Defense, and the FBI Director to leave their position, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The individual must actually leave office and no longer hold their title. An announcement of resignation or intention to leave is not sufficient. The person who held the position at market issuance must be the one who leaves (not a successor). Officials can leave office through resignation, firing, removal, impeachment and removal, or any other process by which they cease to hold the position. A change in the name of an office, including renaming the Secretary of Defense as the Secretary of War, does not constitute leaving that position. The first official to leave triggers resolution for all markets in the set - the one who left resolves to Yes, all others resolve to No.

In the event of death, the market will resolve to the last traded price prior to death, unless such a price is not available, not logically consistent, or not representative of a fair settlement value, in which case the Exchange may determine a fair value in its sole discretion.

markets.rules_primary: If US judicial independence is undermined before Jan 20, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This is defined as any of the following occurring:
An executive order alters the structure of the judiciary. Such an order is considered to alter the judiciary’s structure if it does any of: a) modifies the number, organization, or composition of Article III courts (for example, changing the number of circuits or reassigning judges to different courts) b) changes the scope or limits the jurisdiction of federal courts in a manner that reduces their constitutionally guaranteed authority or c) alters the established procedures for the nomination, confirmation, or lifetime tenure of Article III judges (for example, by replacing lifetime tenure with term limits or otherwise diminishing the constitutional protections afforded to federal judges).
A bill becomes law that undermines judicial independence. Such a bill is considered to do so if it does any of: a) alters the jurisdiction or powers of the federal judiciary in a manner that is inconsistent with the established constitutional framework b) changes the lifetime appointment provisions for Article III judges—such as by replacing lifetime tenure with fixed terms or altering the removal process—thereby diminishing their constitutional protections or c) explicitly removes or materially reduces any protections guaranteed to federal judges under Article III of the Constitution.
Any federal judges are removed outside of the impeachment process – e.g. a federal judge is fired by the Executive, ordered to resign, or any other means than the constitutionally prescribed impeachment process.

Even if any of the above actions are immediately blocked by courts, the market will resolve to Yes.

markets.rules_primary: If the President takes executive action or signs a law that makes at least one complete IVF cycle available at no out-of-pocket cost to patients before Jan 20, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The action must be legally binding and leave patients with no out-of-pocket cost for at least one complete IVF cycle (ovarian stimulation, transfer of the resulting fresh embryos and storage of viable embryos, including medications and procedures). It counts once binding, even if it takes effect later. Full reimbursement of the cycle counts. Coverage may be limited to an eligible group, such as patients diagnosed with infertility or patients of a certain age, as long as a broad class of patients gets the cycle at no cost.

The following do NOT count:
Discounts or lower prices on fertility drugs, including through TrumpRx
Fertility benefits that employers or insurers may choose to offer
Coverage that leaves any copayment, deductible, coinsurance or other patient cost for the cycle
Orders, proposals or recommendations that direct study or future action
markets.title: Will Trump make IVF free?

markets.rules_primary: If the United States has imposed new capital controls in an attempt to limit capital from leaving the United States and going to any country (as opposed to on one specific country) before Jan 20, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Examples of capital controls for the purposes of this Contract include: direct restrictions on outbound transfers (e.g. a regulation requiring government approval or an outright ban on transactions outside of the country above some threshold), asset freeze orders (e.g. ordering banks not to issue cash en masse), setting a rule on the absolute cap of cash that can be physically carried out of the country (as opposed to merely mandating reporting of an amount), foreign exchange purchase limits, and new reporting requirements on capital transfers. 
Restrictions on capital from coming into the United States are not included in the Payout Criterion.
markets.title: Will Trump impose capital controls before 2029?

markets.rules_primary: If Marco Rubio is the first member of the Cabinet of Donald Trump to leave or announce they will leave (such as by quitting, being fired, or being removed from office) after Nov 6, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
If two persons announce they intend to leave at the same time, then the one who leaves first will resolve to Yes and all others will resolve to No. If multiple persons both announce they intend to leave and leave at the same time as other members, then the one whose last name is alphabetically first will resolve to Yes and all others will resolve to No. A person’s announcement of their intent to leave and their departure count as one occurrence, at the earlier of the two. A leave of absence does not constitute leaving the position. Susie Wiles' departure as Chief of Staff, announced on Nov 6, 2026, occurred before Issuance and does not count. 

For purposes of this Contract, the Cabinet includes the heads of the 15 government agencies in the Cabinet as of Issuance, as well as the Administrator of the EPA, the President’s Chief of Staff, Director of National Intelligence, Director of OMB, Director of CIA, United States Trade Representative, Ambassador to the UN, Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers, Administrator of the SBA, and Director of OSTP. Acting roles are not included. Leaving office as a result of death is not encompassed by the Payout Criterion.
